clue.text: Stuck on a couple of pages, then called it a day?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page, so two pages give PP
to call it a day is to stop, so finished, ended

explanation.surface: Someone tacks a couple of pages onto a document and then knocks off for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck on' looks like part of the story about pages, but it is the definition, in the sense of attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attached at the end of a document has been added to it, the sense of the verb in an appendix.

clue.text: Proper to have journalist briefed

parts.note: prim means proper, primly correct in manners
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A prim insistence that the reporter be given a proper briefing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be briefed is to be prepared with information in advance, a synonym of being made ready.

clue.text: Lover dumped on foreign island? One can't feel at home

parts.note: a lover who has been dumped is an ex
île is the French word for island

explanation.surface: A jilted lover consoling themselves on an island abroad, never quite settling in.
explanation.definitionFit: A banished person living away from their own country cannot feel at home; a descriptive definition of a person.

clue.text: Revile girl's father and show anger

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and with the possessive gives DIS
pa is an informal word for father
to rage is to show anger

explanation.surface: Insulting a girl's father and losing one's temper: a family row.
explanation.definitionFit: To revile and to belittle someone are close synonyms: both speak of them with contempt.

clue.text: Carrying gun, did bulge out

indicators.note: the word did carries the gun inside it, holding it between its letters

parts.note: the Sten is a British sub-machine gun

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a weapon finds it makes their clothing bulge.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell or expand outwards from internal pressure is the sense of this verb, a synonym.

clue.text: Bullies are evident in this game

definitions.text: Bullies are evident in this game

parts.words: Bullies are evident in this game
parts.note: a bully, or bully-off, is the way play is started in field ..., not a playground tormentor

explanation.surface: A sport with a reputation for rough, intimidating players.
explanation.walkthrough: Bullies look like thugs, but in field hockey a bully-off is when two players tap sticks to restart play.
explanation.definitionFit: The field sport played with curved sticks starts and restarts play with a bully-off, so bullies appear in it.

clue.text: Criminals — Robin and suchlike primarily?

definitions.meaning: Robin Hood and others with that surname; the question mark admits the playful plural

explanation.definitionFit: Gangsters are hoodlums for short, and the outlaw of Sherwood Forest carries the same word as his surname.

clue.text: Prisoner having got moulded obeyed the rules

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
something moulded has been formed or shaped

explanation.surface: A convict shaped by prison life finally toes the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with rules or standards is to fall into line with them, a synonym of obeying.

clue.text: Close shave leader avoided running to ground

indicators.note: the first letter of the phrase is dodged, so it is dropped

parts.note: a close shave is a near thing, a narrow escape

explanation.surface: A narrow escape while running away to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader avoided' drops the N from NEAR THING, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In electrics a wire run to the ground is grounded; in hunting a fox driven to its den is run to earth.

clue.text: A hundred and one restrictions in places like London

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one
ties are bonds or restrictions

explanation.surface: Pointing out that a hundred and one restrictions apply in big metropolises.
explanation.definitionFit: London is an example of a large urban centre, and the definition asks for examples of such places.

clue.text: People who scoff in this corner shop

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words this corner shop

explanation.surface: Mocking customers hang around the local corner shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to jeer or mock, so people who scoff are mockers who treat things with contempt.

clue.text: Influence of bank probed by newspaper

indicators.note: the bank is entered by the newspaper, which goes inside it

parts.note: a levee is an embankment along a river
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper investigates the sway a bank holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial but is the river embankment, LEVEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Power to sway outcomes, as in having clout over someone, is a synonym of influence.

clue.text: Calm down male faced with something falling down chimney?

indicators.note: the male has the other piece in front of it, facing it

parts.note: soot falls down a chimney
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man trying to stay calm when a cloud of black dust drops down the chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or settle someone's agitation is the meaning; a direct synonym for calming.

clue.text: Flattery? The blind man's put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of the phrase are disordered

explanation.surface: Is it flattery, when the blind man is upset?
explanation.definitionFit: Coaxing flattery used to persuade someone is a synonym; the question mark marks the definition-led surface.

clue.text: Belt making bonier lad look silly

indicators.note: letters made to look silly are jumbled into a foolish order

explanation.surface: A belt worn by a skinny boy makes him look ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder belt with loops or pockets for cartridges is a kind of belt, so this is an example.

clue.text: Left-wing party is beginning to threaten

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering

indicators.note: the beginning of the word threaten means only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A left-wing political party is starting to make threats.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of collective ownership is politically on the left, so the adjective matches left-wing.

clue.text: Settle in work mostly wearing coat

indicators.note: the coat is worn round the work, which goes inside it

parts.note: to plate is to coat with metal, so plate is a coat

indicators.note: most of the word, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: opus is Latin for a work, especially a musical one

explanation.surface: Settling down to work, mostly while wearing a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' looks like a garment, but it is the verb plate, as in coating with metal; 'mostly' drops the S of the Latin work.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a land is to fill it with inhabitants, so the verbs are synonyms in the colonising sense.

clue.text: Allowed granny to go to church — that's mattered, getting outside

indicators.note: the counted word gets outside the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: something that has mattered has counted
nan is an informal word for grandmother
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Granny was allowed to go to church, which mattered to her.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate or sanction something is to approve it, so this past tense means allowed.

clue.text: Hoary worker hugging citizen that's lost a lot of heart

indicators.note: the worker hugs the other piece, splitting round it

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's usual worker

indicators.note: the central letters of the word citizen are removed, most of its heart

explanation.surface: A grizzled old labourer embraces a fellow citizen who has lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost a lot of heart' removes TIZ from CITIZEN, leaving CIEN, which ANT hugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoary means grey with age, so very old; a synonym.

clue.text: Something very small supporting a big mass?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
a ton is a large unit of mass

explanation.surface: A tiny thing propping up something enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle in the nucleus of an atom is a tiny thing, an example.

clue.text: Smell attached to old biblical city? That's funny!

definitions.note: a noun phrase is wanted: that which is funny, comedy

parts.note: a hum is informal British for a bad smell
Ur of the Chaldees, Abraham's home, is the crossword's favourite biblical city

explanation.surface: A smell clinging to an ancient biblical site raises a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is the quality of what is funny, so the exclamation points to the comic quality itself.

clue.text: Prepared to study before getting Third in Physics

indicators.note: the study comes before the next letter

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

indicators.note: the third letter of the word Physics

explanation.surface: Revising before ending up with a third-class degree in Physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared means being set for action, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Opportunist, unknown character in court

parts.note: a chancer is an opportunist who takes risks
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An opportunistic, mysterious character appears in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is a branch of the English High Court, so it names a court.

clue.text: Famous wedding venue overlooking lake or some other waterway

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits above the other, overlooking it

parts.note: Cana in Galilee was where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding

explanation.surface: A celebrated wedding location with views of a lake or other waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made channel for boats is a waterway, a type other than a lake.

clue.text: Wicked home with time for witty conversation

parts.note: bad means wicked
in means at home
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A disreputable household where the time goes on clever banter.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful, witty banter between people is the meaning, a synonym of repartee.

clue.text: Fire in one holiday cottage accommodating any number

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the cottage takes in the number, holding it inside

parts.note: a gîte is a French holiday cottage
N is the mathematical symbol for any number

explanation.surface: A blaze in a holiday cottage that sleeps any number of guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To set alight is to kindle a fire, so the verb means fire in the sense of setting off.

clue.text: End of May — before the usual time for annual to appear

indicators.note: the end of the word May is its last letter

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: A flowering annual comes up ahead of schedule, at the end of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annual' looks like a plant in the surface but is the adjective meaning once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening once every year is an adjective synonym.

clue.text: What sounds like rubbish provided by Heather gossiping

indicators.note: a word that is said the same way as the rubbish word

parts.note: tat is cheap, worthless stuff, rubbish
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: Rubbish talked by someone called Heather amounts to tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Chattering idly about others' affairs is a synonym of telling tales.
